prompt: What happened out there — which parts of the fence got damaged?
why_it_changes_work: The whole scope: a few sections vs. the full line is different work, different crew, different quote.
skip_if: Customer says skip, doesn't know, or gives no answer.
default: Storm damage, full fence line affected.

prompt: Roughly how much fence are we talking? Feet, or just 'about a backyard' is fine.
why_it_changes_work: Drives material quantities and whether one crew finishes in a day.
skip_if: Customer says skip or can't estimate.

prompt: Who's getting the materials — you or the contractor?
why_it_changes_work: Splits every quote into labor-only vs. labor-plus-materials; without it, quotes can't be compared.
skip_if: Customer says skip or doesn't know.

prompt: Got a budget range in mind? Ballpark is fine.
why_it_changes_work: A range steers the SOW away from work the customer won't pay for.
skip_if: Customer says skip or prefers not to say.
default: No stated budget — quotes will define it.

prompt: When do you need this done by?
why_it_changes_work: A hard deadline is the difference between a quote and a bid.
skip_if: Customer says skip or whenever works.

prompt: How will you know when it's done right — what would you check?
why_it_changes_work: Acceptance criteria: the customer's own words go into the completion terms.
default: Fence straight, panels secure, gates work.

prompt: Getting quotes from a few contractors, or just this one?
why_it_changes_work: Determines whether the SOW needs line-item granularity for apples-to-apples comparison.

prompt: Anything you definitely don't want done?
why_it_changes_work: Exclusions belong in the SOW, not in a dispute afterward.
